note: Forest Service campground on both banks of the Rockcastle River off KY 192, about 18 miles west of London, with wooded sites below the Bee Rock cliffs. The sites sit under trees with the river in view, and a CCC-built footbridge links the two sides. A 23-ft rig is at the upper end of the 'small RVs' the Forest Service names; no pad lengths are posted. Low-lying parts flood in high water. Boat ramp on the Laurel County side; the Bee Rock Loop and Rockcastle Narrows trails start here. --Claude
summary: Kept with a size caveat. 25 first-come sites ($15, doubles $20), no hookups, vault toilets, faucets (off in winter); Laurel side 17-25 open all year, Pulaski side 1-16 March-November; no rec.gov listing. Riverview confirmed (sites under canopy along the river). Unsourced access-road warning dropped from the note.
flags: WATERFRONT: riverview CONFIRMED. The guide map puts sites 5-16 (Pulaski side) and 17-25 (Laurel side) along the Rockcastle River (~60-80 m wide), but imagery shows both banks under continuous canopy with no open apron, so the sites are a view. No upgrade.

SIZE: the FS page says 'sites for both small RVs and tents' and posts no pad lengths. Kept under the unclear-pad-size rule with the caveat in the note. Reviewer may want a phone check with the London Ranger District if anything stricter than 'small RVs' is wanted.

ACCESS: the old note's 'access road has narrow/bumpy stretches near the river' and 'call before bringing anything bigger' appear on no agency page read; the FS page and guide say nothing about road limits (guide: 'Campground speed limit is 10 MPH'). Dropped from the note; not a drop candidate.
